label: Slovenská bryndza
note: Slovak PGI: up to 50% cow lump cheese

about.text: Slovenská bryndza is a Slovak PGI cheese: ground sheep lump cheese, or sheep lump cheese mixed with up to 50% cow lump cheese, with salt (OJ C 232/2007).

how.text: Slovak bryndza is not made from milk directly. Sheep lump cheese (hrudkový syr) is made in the hut, then ripened and ground with salt at the bryndza dairy. The PGI lets the sheep lump cheese be mixed with up to 50 % cow lump cheese. Its acid and flavour come from the wild lactic flora of the raw milk, not from a bought starter.

steps.name: wash
steps.note: The lump cheese is sorted and washed with water.
Over 3,700 isolates in one study came from the raw milk and the dairy, not from a starter; they include L. paraplantarum, Enterococcus hirae, Enterococcus faecalis and Pediococcus acidilactici.
The pulp is salted and spread on rollers.

processing.text: The lump cheese is ripened before it is ground with salt; the flora comes from the raw milk and the dairy, not a starter.

facts.v: Lump cheese is 100 % sheep, or mixed with up to 50 % cow
Sheep milk is 'sweetened' (set) at the mountain hut; the lump cheese is dried there and taken to the bryndziarna (bryndza dairy)
Slovak PGI; production area is the mountainous part of Slovakia
